content:
anya: heads up — hosted API (us-west) p99 spiked to ~1.6s at 09:12 UTC, correlated with a jump in queue_depth on gpu-pool-3. root logs: `queue_depth=179, active_batches=12, avg_batch_size=11`

mike: seeing it on graphs too. p95 moved from 220ms -> 680ms. batch_size distribution collapsed (many tiny batches).

liz: quick profiler dump shows a flurry of short-request churn and kernel-selector switching to aux-kernel-2 around the spike window. suspect batching fragmentation + kselector fallback. attaching grep of traces:```
[09:11:58] req A seq=16 -> primary-kernel
[09:12:01] req B seq=6  -> aux-kernel-2 (fallback)
[09:12:02] kernel-selector: transition because batch_size < 12 for 3 consecutive samples
```

yuto: KV cache metrics show an eviction storm on tenant:hotshard-17 at same time — high prefix miss rate and frequent prefetch churn. possible noisy neighbor (tenant) causing workload to fragment caches and reduce batch coalescing.

mike: that aligns. if KV cache miss increases, many requests hit 'short' path where seq len small and kernel selector chooses lower-throughput kernel. Means more kernels and lower batch sizes -> latency tail.

sam: rolling stats: `kvcache_evictions/min` jumped 8x, `coalesce_wait_ms` increased variance (p99 ~ 14ms). Batcher max_wait is 12ms in this pool.

anya: immediate mitigations?

liz: quick wins: 1) temporarily route traffic for hotshard-17 to dedicated pool (if allowed) OR 2) widen coalesce window to 18ms for gpu-pool-3 to allow larger batches during bursts. 3) throttle tenant at rate-limiter for noisy tenant.

yuto: routing to dedicated is safest for stability but needs approval. I can flip a routing rule to avoid affected GPU nodes (takes ~2min).

mike: also suggest bumping batcher min_batch_size threshold to avoid premature kernel-selector fallback for tiny batches (e.g., min_batch_size=8 -> 6?). Caveat: could increase latency for single-user flows.

infra-bot: deploy queued: routing-change/v2 -> prod-gpu-pool (PR #4872). ETA ~4m.

sam: I'm running an on-the-fly flamegraph for kernel hotpaths, attaching output link: https://internal.perf/graphs/3210004567 (no external access). shows kernel launch overhead increases when batch_size < 12.

liz: if we widen coalesce window to 18ms, we should also lower the prefetch aggressiveness to avoid further KV churn. prefetch rate currently set to 200r/s for that pool — reduce to 80r/s temporarily.

anya: owners: yuto -> flip routing; liz -> temp coalesce + prefetch change; mike -> adjust batcher heuristic and observe; sam -> perf trace monitoring. post updates in thread.

[yuto updated routing at 09:15 UTC]
yuto: routing change applied. gpu-pool-3 now excludes nodes g3-*-hotshard.

[liz updated batcher config at 09:17 UTC]
liz: coalesce_window_ms=18, prefetch_rate=80r/s pushed to pool config.

mike: pushed temporary kernel-selector lower_threshold tweak (min_batch_size override = 6) to staging; will roll to prod in 5m if no regressions.

sam: metrics post mitigations (09:22-09:30): queue_depth back to ~30, p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 320ms, avg_batch_size rebounded to 36. kvcache_evictions down 70%.

anya: nice. keep monitoring for 1h. if stable, we'll keep routing for 24h and schedule a follow-up to harden kernel-selector heuristics and tenant isolation.

mike: TODOs for follow-up: 1) add a kvcache eviction alert tied to batcher fragmentation signature, 2) add a short-path kernel performance microbenchmark, 3) consider per-tenant soft QoS to avoid hotshard eviction storms.

liz: I'll draft an RFC for kernel-selector fallback thresholds + safer coalesce dynamic scaling.

anya: thanks team. marking as triaged — reopen if spike returns. :thumbsup:
